newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: CSM 96/97 NET SEEN UP AROUND 10 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: CSM 96/97 NET SEEN UP AROUND 10 PERCENT.

text.p: Dutch food group CSM NV will post a solid rise of some 10 percent in 1996/97 first half profits on Thursday, with the firm's ingredients division still driving growth, analysts said on Monday.
They expect the group to report net profit in the six months to end-March of between 100 and 106 million guilders, with most estimates around 104 million.
CSM posted net profit of 93.5 million guilders in the first half of 1995/96, up 8.2 percent from the same year-earlier period.

The company groups its operations into three divisions of food, sugar and ingredients. In February it predicted turnover in the ingredients division would grow by 45 percent to around 1.6 billion guilders in the 1996/97 financial year.

Turnover in the food division was seen increasing to around 1.4 billion guilders from 1.3 billion, while the sugar division would continue contributing good profits, but was not expected to grow, it said.

"Ingredients are the main engine of growth and will continue to be so for some 12 months, after that there may be some space for growth on the confectionery side, in the food division," said ING Barings analyst Gerard Rijk.

Rijk said first-half sales would rise quite strongly, by about 20 percent, due to the impact of recent acquisitions, with earnings up by around 12 percent. Currency gains would account for about three percent of the profit rise, he said.
CSM bought U.S. bakery ingredients maker Karp's Inc. in early February and finalised the takeover of Scandinavian sweets maker Malaco in March.

"When you look at those, you could expect a higher earnings figure for the half year, but management have made clear they will not show more than a 10 percent rise in earnings, because they feel they are not able to show more than that in the long run," analyst Lambert Oorthuizen of Amstgeld said.
Growth would be flat in both the sugar and foods division over the half, he said, with expansion coming primarily from the U.S. bakery ingredients and lactic acid supply businesses.
"That's the growth part of the company and they will invest in the future in that part of the firm." -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
